This is not an Islamic country.

Should a restaurant in Britain be free to choose its own menu? Yes or no 👇

posts.text:
I’ve decided to leave NVIDIA. There are a few things I want to say.

As a robotics engineer at NVIDIA, I have seen Jensen as much more than the company’s CEO.

I admire his willingness to invest in a future that was not yet obvious. He committed to CUDA long before the deep learning boom and positioned NVIDIA for AI before it became everyone’s priority. Those decisions helped build the infrastructure that powers today’s AI.

I have seen that same vision in physical AI: investing in robotics, sharing open-source tools and projects, and building computing platforms that bring AI into the physical world. This is the work I do every day—and a future I believe in.

But what matters most to me is the culture he helped build.

Engineers are encouraged to explore, take risks, and learn from mistakes. Jensen reads employees’ Top 5 emails, follows their work, and engages directly. In a company this large, that connection matters. It makes an individual engineer feel that their ideas can still be heard.

That is why this has been so disappointing.

I do not have all the facts surrounding the allegations, and I cannot prejudge the investigation. My admiration for Jensen does not put him above scrutiny.

What I find difficult to accept is having to come to terms with his departure before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it. What this means for our direction, our culture, and the people doing the work remains unclear to me.

I have felt that engineers’ perspectives matter here. On this decision, I have not felt heard. That gap has been more painful than I expected.

I understand that some information cannot be shared immediately. But that does not erase the feeling of being left outside a decision that affects the company we help build every day.

A company’s greatness comes from its leadership, its governance, and the people who turn its ambitions into reality. Employees’ trust and sense of belonging are part of that, too.

Jensen’s vision and the engineering culture he shaped were important reasons I wanted to stay. His departure led me to decide that my own chapter here should also come to a close.

I leave with sadness and gratitude. The colleagues I have worked with, and the work we believed in together, will always matter to me.

These are my personal views.

posts.text:
Man and woman in 20s killed after a car being pursued by police crashes into them in Leeds as multiple arrests made

Police are continuing to investigate the double fatal road traffic collision in Leeds which has tragically claimed the lives of two people.

The incident happened at around 12.44am this morning (Sunday) when a blue BMW 123D failed to stop for a police vehicle on Gelderd Road.

Officers began a pursuit, during which the BMW was involved in a collision with a white Volkswagen Scirocco that was turning onto Gelderd Road from Lowfields Road.

Tragically, the driver of the Volkswagen, a 22-year-old man from York, was pronounced dead at the scene. His passenger, a 23-year-old woman, also from York, was taken to hospital but sadly died a short time later.

A 39-year-old man from Harrogate has been arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving and driving while over the prescribed limit for cannabis. He remains in police custody.

Three other occupants of the BMW, two boys aged 16 and 17 and a 16-year-old girl, were taken to hospital with injuries not believed to be life-threatening. All three have also been arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving.

A police scene and road closure remain in place on Gelderd Road, with motorists advised to avoid the area and use alternative routes.

A referral has been made to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC), which has declared an independent investigation into the incident.

Police are appealing for anyone who witnessed the collision or may have relevant dashcam footage to come forward.

posts.text:
Let me educate some mischievous persons who try to equate singing the ON YOUR MANDATE song, which is used to serenade President Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, with singing an outlawed anthem IN PLACE of a legally approved National Anthem.

At no time have supporters of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu sung ON YOUR MANDATE IN PLACE of the National Anthem. At every occasion, the NATIONAL ANTHEM is always sung as a mark of recognition of one of our most important national symbols, and then the President is serenaded by his supporters with _ON YOUR MANDATE.

Nobody stops Peter Obi from adopting a song, even the old anthem, as his own song. But it must be sung either before or AFTER the legally recognised National Anthem is given its due RECOGNITION.

Again, as part of presidential protocol, whenever the President walks into an event or gets up to speak, the Police Band usually plays ANY instrumental to herald his presence or speech. They simply choose anyone they fancy. Check all videos of Presidents Obasanjo, Yar'Adua, Jonathan or Buhari entering the National Assembly or getting up to speak. It must be preceded by an instrumental from the Police Band. In this case, the Police Band sometimes plays the ON YOUR MANDATE instrumental to herald the President's speech. This comes AFTER THE NATIONAL ANTHEM has been played.

Since MAGA is so concerned about immigrants coming to America “the right way” — let’s talk about Melania Trump:

Melania obtained U.S. permanent residency (a green card) in 2001 through an EB-1 visa, often dubbed the "Einstein visa," which is reserved for individuals with "extraordinary abilities" in sciences, arts, education, business, or athletics. 

As a model, she was one of only five people from Slovenia to receive the visa that year. 

The EB-1 visa requires applicants to prove "sustained national or international acclaim.” Applicants must either have a major, one-time award (like a Nobel Prize or Oscar) or meet at least 3 out of 10 criteria, such as:

✅ Published material about the individual.
✅ Performances in leading roles.
✅ Commercial success (e.g., modeling work/billboards).

MANY people, including Rep. Jasmine Crockett, have questioned how Melania possibly met these high standards compared to top-tier international celebrities that have been rejected.

Just so coincidentally, Melania — unlike the others — was planning a wedding to Donald Trump.
